extracted.intended_audience: research funders, academic institutions, peer reviewers, policymakers, and researchers interested in gender equity in grant peer review
extracted.subtask_short: reducing gender bias in grant review
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and recommended actions for recognizing, measuring, and reducing gender bias in research grant peer review processes, and for aligning peer-review reforms with broader institutional gender-equity policies. Targets funders, reviewers, and academic leaders designing or evaluating grant review systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize gender bias as systemic and institutionalized
rubrics_metrics.description: Gender bias within the research grant review process worldwide is a manifestation of historical and systemic gender bias within academic institutions and beyond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand bias as embedded in 'policies, practices, beliefs and written or unwritten rules of behaviour' and intersecting with race, class, sexuality and other markers of difference; reforms should target institutional structures as well as review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruct reviewers to focus on 'the science' not 'the scientist'
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should be directed to assess 'the science' of a proposal instead of 'the scientist.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence (Witteman et al.) shows that instructing reviewers to focus on the proposal's science can reduce gender bias in funding decisions; reviewer guidance and scoring frameworks should emphasize proposal content over applicant identity or perceived leadership ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect both quantitative and qualitative evidence on gender bias
rubrics_metrics.description: More evidence, both quantitative and qualitative, is needed: quantitative data to understand the scale of the problem and qualitative exploration to understand motivations, incentives and reasoning underpinning gender bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design monitoring and evaluation plans that include statistics on application outcomes disaggregated by gender and other axes, plus qualitative studies (e.g., interviews, focus groups) to reveal reviewer reasoning and systemic incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement institutional policies to support caregiving and work–life balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic institutions should have policies such as flexible working hours, adequate parental leave and child care facilities to support both women and men who need to raise and care for their families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding agencies and institutions should adopt or require family-friendly policies because lack of such supports contributes to women's reduced time for research and grant preparation; consider policy adoption as part of equity strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for disproportionate service and mentoring burdens on women
rubrics_metrics.description: Women are frequently asked to sit on committees and perform service work, leaving less time for their own research and grant preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and promotion/funding evaluators should recognize and adjust for service loads (including mentoring and committee work) so that service demands do not penalize research productivity; institutions should track and mitigate unequal service distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust assessment of productivity to account for citation and coauthorship biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Women are underrepresented as authors, are less frequently cited than men, and may suffer a 'coauthor penalty' when group-authored work leads to reduced recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using metrics like publications and citations in funding decisions, account for systemic citation gaps and collaboration-credit disparities (e.g., avoid assuming male coauthors took the lead); consider qualitative assessment of contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize intersectional analysis and responses
rubrics_metrics.description: How these processes affect women of colour, Indigenous women and academics from low-income countries is underexplored and should be a priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disaggregate data and design interventions that consider intersecting axes of disadvantage (race, Indigeneity, country income level) rather than treating 'women' as a homogeneous group; fund targeted research and policy responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use institutional incentives such as gender-equity awards (e.g., Athena SWAN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award-based programs (such as Athena SWAN) recognize universities' recruitment, promotion and retention of women; certain biomedical funding is tied to Athena SWAN awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funders can incentivize institutional change by tying eligibility or preferential support to recognized gender-equity programs, thereby institutionalizing and incentivizing progress toward parity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase women's representation in leadership, conferences and decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Women are underrepresented at higher levels of academic hierarchies and within academic conferences and colloquia, limiting networking and career advancement opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funders and institutions should promote gender-balanced leadership and speaking opportunities, and avoid overburdening the limited number of female leaders with service requests that reduce their time for research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund targeted research on gender and diversity in academic funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding agencies (e.g., NIH, European Commission) should launch calls for research into gender and diversity in academic funding and research practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support both evaluative studies of peer review processes and intervention trials (e.g., quasi-experimental designs) to identify effective strategies to reduce bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align peer-review reforms with broader institutional transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts to overhaul processes of research grant peer review must go hand in hand with larger projects of transformation within academia aimed at shifting traditional gender norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine procedural changes in peer review (e.g., reviewer instructions, assessment criteria) with institutional policies and cultural-change initiatives to achieve sustained, systemic change in equity of funding outcomes.
